item: A long gate hold in the storage-events journal carries what its holder thread was doing in the kernel (ws, gap), counted once a second from /proc, paid for by writing frames at their measured width
refs: coordinator 17 Oct; OSM gate census REPORT section 2
summary: The 16 Oct holds of 30 to 182 s could not be told apart as slow work or a stalled thread. holder_state looks at the holder once a second while a hold is past 30 s and already journaled (3 small /proc reads, 29 microseconds, on the watchdog thread) and counts six classes: running, runnable, futex, nap (SQLite's busy handler), disk, other; gap is the longest time between two looks. The first look counts nothing (it is the baseline); the thread's name and the kernel symbol are never kept; off Linux the hold says ws null with ws_why unsupported-os; counts reach the journal at the 15 s tick and at the release, not once a second. futex is a floor for GIL waits (a look hands the GIL to its only waiter). Bytes: 58 per hold at the widest, paid by writer.FRAME_CHARS = 90, the measured maximum of module:function:line under src/ (79), pinned against every function by an AST walk, which frees 4,200 bytes the model counted for frames no real event has; the widest journal is 123,837 bytes with all 20 splits (1,163 free; ordinary names 83,327), the fixed part 5,176 to 5,831. Also fixes a flake: the phase tests counted samples of the module's gate while the process's own watchdog thread could tick in the same hold (about 8 per cent of runs).
